```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

cfg <- params$cfg
stopifnot(!is.null(cfg))   # render through run_infercnv.R so that params are passed
```

Runs inferCNV separately for each sample. The per-sample choices (cells included, reference groups, Leiden resolution) are listed in `infercnv_samples.csv`. All other settings are the same for every sample. The original code, with one section per sample, is kept in `original/InferCNV_original.Rmd`.

# Attached libraries
```{r}
library(infercnv)
library(dplyr)
library(SeuratObject)   # FetchData(); as attached in the original session (sessionInfo/)
```

# Preparing input files
## 1-Gene_order_position.txt file
Gene_order_position file: chromosome, start, and stop position for each gene, tab-delimited.
It was made once from the 10x Genomics reference GTF (refdata-gex-GRCh38-2020-A, `genes.gtf`) with `gtf_to_position_file.py` from the inferCNV repository (https://github.com/broadinstitute/infercnv/blob/master/scripts/gtf_to_position_file.py), using gene names to match the count matrix. It is included with the code (`gene_order_file` in `config.yml`).

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
python gtf_to_position_file.py --attribute_name gene_name genes.gtf gene_positions.txt
```

## 2-Raw counts matrix for Genes X Cells
```{r}
sts.simspec <- readRDS(cfg$integrated_object)
sts_counts <- sts.simspec@assays$RNA@counts
```

# Samples
```{r samples, results="markup"}
runs <- read.csv(cfg$samples_csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
if (!identical(cfg$samples, "all")) {
  stopifnot(all(cfg$samples %in% runs$sample))
  runs <- runs[runs$sample %in% cfg$samples, ]
}
runs[, c("sample", "subset_by", "cell_classes", "ref_groups", "leiden_resolution", "up_to_step")]

annotation.dir <- file.path(params$step_dir, "annotations")
dir.create(annotation.dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Run inferCNV per sample
```{r run_infercnv}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(runs))) {
  r <- runs[i, ]
  message(">>> ", format(Sys.time()), " inferCNV for ", r$sample)

  cell.classes <- strsplit(r$cell_classes, ";")[[1]]
  ref.groups   <- strsplit(r$ref_groups, ";")[[1]]

  # cells of this sample (or patient) in the selected classes
  md    <- sts.simspec[[]]
  cells <- colnames(sts.simspec)[which(md[[r$subset_by]] == r$sample &
                                       md$simspec_cell_class %in% cell.classes)]

  df <- FetchData(sts.simspec, vars = c("Cell_Ids", "simspec_cell_class"), cells = cells)
  annotation.file <- file.path(annotation.dir, r$annotation_file)
  write.table(df, file = annotation.file, sep = '\t', quote = F, row.names = F, col.names = F) # this is a correct format

  infercnv_obj = CreateInfercnvObject(raw_counts_matrix = as.matrix(sts_counts),
                                      annotations_file = annotation.file,
                                      delim = "\t",
                                      gene_order_file = cfg$gene_order_file,
                                      ref_group_names = ref.groups
                                      )

  # No seed is set, as in the original run: subclusters and HMM calls vary between runs (see README)
  inferCNV.subclusters <- infercnv::run(infercnv_obj,
    cutoff = 0.1, # key, and recommened set = 0.1 for 10X data
    out_dir = file.path(params$step_dir, r$out_name),
    cluster_by_groups = T, # to perform separate clustering for the tumor cells according to the patient type, as defined in the cell annotations file. Set this T if we want to look at each malignant sample separately
    analysis_mode = 'subclusters',
    denoise = T, # enable denoise procedure
    HMM = T, # enable CNV prediction
    noise_logistic = TRUE,
    sd_amplifier = 3,
    BayesMaxPNormal = 0.3, # default is 0.5, we can reduce this to filter out low confident CNV prediction
    tumor_subcluster_pval = 0.05,
    leiden_resolution = r$leiden_resolution, # per sample, to reduce the number of subclusters before the HMM step
    up_to_step = if (is.na(r$up_to_step)) 100 else r$up_to_step # 100 is the inferCNV default (all steps)
  )

  rm(infercnv_obj, inferCNV.subclusters, df)
  gc()
}
```
